rationale_overall: This week's pool is dominated by noise that doesn't survive the investability filter: private companies with no US ticker (SpaceX/Starship coverage across multiple articles, Blue Origin TeraWave and lunar-lander pivot, Ricursive Intelligence's $300M raise), foreign government/defense programs with no liquid US line (Turkey's unmanned fighter jet, India's DRDO hypersonic missile unveiling, Norway's Hanwha Chunmoo deal), keyword false-matches (Doc Martens x Metallica 'Rocket' boots, Shiveluch volcano 'VA' advisory, Rocket City Retro Fest, a robotics youth tournament), and generic AI-adoption op-eds with no ticker angle (Pope Leo on AI, ISESCO, UW-Eau Claire panel, India's Economic Survey, Ohio deepfake law gaps). The one real commercial catalyst worth noting -- BlackSky's Gen-3 satellite-intelligence contract expansion -- is a genuine geopolitical/rockets-adjacent buildup signal but is a single incremental contract story, not the kind of clearly-stronger rising vehicle that should displace an existing core holding (GOOGL, NVDA, RKLB, SMR) on a weekly cadence; it's one to keep watching, not act on yet. Uranium-week bullish sentiment reinforces the existing SMR nuclear thesis rather than arguing for a new ticker. Rocket Lab's dual headlines (Neutron fairing arrival vs. a Congressional funding-risk piece on a possible $4B payday) roughly offset and don't rise to a thesis breach. Per the swap-only-on-genuine-catalyst instruction, holding the watchlist unchanged this week.
